title: Supabase Postgres Best Practices
summary: Skill manifest for a comprehensive Postgres performance optimization guide organized into 8 priority categories (query, connection, security, schema, locking, data, monitoring, advanced) maintained by Supabase.
key_facts: 8 rule categories by priority: query (CRITICAL), conn (CRITICAL), security (CRITICAL), schema (HIGH), lock (MEDIUM-HIGH), data (MEDIUM), monitor (LOW-MEDIUM), advanced (LOW). Version 1.1.1, January 2026.

title: Writing Guidelines for Postgres References
summary: Internal authoring guide for contributors creating Postgres best-practice reference files, covering structure, SQL formatting standards, impact level classifications, and review checklist.
key_facts: Impact scale: CRITICAL=10-100x, HIGH=5-20x, MEDIUM-HIGH=2-5x, MEDIUM=1.5-3x, LOW-MEDIUM=1.2-2x. Error-first structure required.

title: Section Definitions
summary: Defines the 8 rule category sections and their filename prefixes used to auto-assign Postgres best-practice rules within the skill.
key_facts: Filename prefix mapping: query-, conn-, security-, schema-, lock-, data-, monitor-, advanced-.

title: Clear, Action-Oriented Title (e.g., Use Partial Indexes for Filtered Queries)
summary: Blank template with YAML frontmatter and markdown skeleton for creating new Postgres best-practice reference files.
key_facts: Template frontmatter fields: title, impact, impactDescription, tags. Body structure: explanation, Incorrect SQL, Correct SQL, optional context, reference link.

title: Use tsvector for Full-Text Search
summary: Explains why LIKE-based search is unindexable and shows how to use generated tsvector columns with GIN indexes for 100x faster full-text search with ranking support.
key_facts: Use generated always stored tsvector column + GIN index; to_tsquery supports AND (&), OR (|), prefix (:*) operators; 100x faster than LIKE.

title: Index JSONB Columns for Efficient Querying
summary: Covers GIN indexing strategies for JSONB columns including operator class selection (jsonb_ops vs jsonb_path_ops) and expression indexes for key-specific lookups.
key_facts: jsonb_path_ops is 2-3x smaller than jsonb_ops but only supports @> operator; expression index on (attributes->>'brand') for equality lookups; 10-100x speedup.

title: Configure Idle Connection Timeouts
summary: Shows how to reclaim idle connection slots using idle_in_transaction_session_timeout and idle_session_timeout server settings plus PgBouncer-level equivalents.
key_facts: idle_in_transaction_session_timeout='30s' and idle_session_timeout='10min' recommended; PgBouncer: server_idle_timeout=60, client_idle_timeout=300; can reclaim 30-50% of slots.

title: Set Appropriate Connection Limits
summary: Explains how to size max_connections and work_mem based on available RAM to prevent memory exhaustion and database crashes.
key_facts: Formula: max_connections=(RAM_MB/5)-reserved; for 4GB RAM recommend 100 connections; work_mem*max_connections should not exceed 25% of RAM; each connection uses 1-3MB.

title: Use Connection Pooling for All Applications
summary: Explains the cost of per-request Postgres connections and demonstrates PgBouncer transaction-mode pooling to handle 10-100x more concurrent users with fewer actual connections.
key_facts: Pool size formula: (CPU_cores*2)+spindle_count; transaction mode returns connection after each txn; session mode required for prepared statements and temp tables; CRITICAL impact.

title: Use Prepared Statements Correctly with Pooling
summary: Explains why named prepared statements fail in transaction-mode pooling and provides three workarounds: unnamed statements, DEALLOCATE after use, or session-mode pooling.
key_facts: Node.js pg: {prepare:false} to disable; JDBC: prepareThreshold=0; Supabase uses port 5432 for session mode vs 6543 for transaction mode.

title: Batch INSERT Statements for Bulk Data
summary: Shows how to replace individual INSERT statements with multi-row batches or COPY command for 10-50x faster bulk data loading.
key_facts: Batch up to ~1000 rows per INSERT statement; COPY command is fastest for bulk loading from CSV or stdin; 10-50x speedup.

title: Eliminate N+1 Queries with Batch Loading
summary: Shows how to replace per-item query loops with single batch queries using ANY(array[...]) or JOINs to reduce 100+ round trips to a single database call.
key_facts: Use WHERE id = ANY($1::bigint[]) to pass array from application; or use LEFT JOIN instead of loop; 10-100x fewer round trips.

title: Use Cursor-Based Pagination Instead of OFFSET
summary: Explains why OFFSET pagination degrades on deep pages and shows keyset/cursor pagination pattern using WHERE id > last_id for consistent O(1) performance.
key_facts: OFFSET pagination scans all skipped rows; cursor pagination is O(1) regardless of page depth; multi-column sort cursors must include all sort columns.

title: Use UPSERT for Insert-or-Update Operations
summary: Demonstrates INSERT ... ON CONFLICT as an atomic upsert alternative to the check-then-insert race condition pattern.
key_facts: INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (col) DO UPDATE SET ... RETURNING * is atomic; DO NOTHING variant for insert-or-ignore; eliminates race conditions.

title: Use Advisory Locks for Application-Level Locking
summary: Explains advisory locks as a lightweight coordination mechanism and shows session-level, transaction-level, and try-lock patterns using pg_advisory_lock functions.
key_facts: pg_advisory_xact_lock auto-releases on commit/rollback; pg_try_advisory_lock is non-blocking; use hashtext() to convert string keys to bigint lock IDs.

title: Prevent Deadlocks with Consistent Lock Ordering
summary: Shows how to eliminate deadlocks by acquiring row locks in consistent (e.g., ID ascending) order using SELECT ... FOR UPDATE before updating, and how to detect deadlocks via pg_stat_database.
key_facts: SELECT * FROM accounts WHERE id IN (1,2) ORDER BY id FOR UPDATE acquires locks in safe order; single UPDATE with CASE expression is deadlock-free; check deadlocks with pg_stat_database.

title: Keep Transactions Short to Reduce Lock Contention
summary: Explains why long transactions (especially those with external API calls mid-transaction) cause lock contention and shows how to minimize transaction scope to milliseconds.
key_facts: Do API calls outside transaction boundaries; use statement_timeout='30s' to abort runaway queries; 3-5x throughput improvement possible.

title: Use SKIP LOCKED for Non-Blocking Queue Processing
summary: Shows the FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED pattern for parallel worker queues where multiple workers can each claim a different pending job without blocking each other.
key_facts: Atomic claim-and-update: UPDATE ... WHERE id=(SELECT id ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED) RETURNING *; 10x queue throughput; avoids worker contention.

title: Use EXPLAIN ANALYZE to Diagnose Slow Queries
summary: Demonstrates EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS, FORMAT TEXT) usage and how to interpret key plan node types such as Seq Scan, high buffer reads, and external sort to identify performance bottlenecks.
key_facts: Seq Scan on large table = missing index; Buffers: read >> hit = data not cached; external merge sort = work_mem too low; use EXPLAIN ANALYZE not just EXPLAIN.

title: Enable pg_stat_statements for Query Analysis
summary: Shows how to enable pg_stat_statements extension and query it for slowest-by-total-time, most-frequent, and high-mean-latency queries to identify optimization candidates.
key_facts: CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS pg_stat_statements; query total_exec_time, mean_exec_time, calls columns; reset with pg_stat_statements_reset(); flag queries with mean_exec_time>100ms.

title: Maintain Table Statistics with VACUUM and ANALYZE
summary: Explains how stale planner statistics cause wrong query plans and shows manual ANALYZE usage, autovacuum tuning for high-churn tables, and how to inspect last-vacuum timestamps.
key_facts: Tune autovacuum per-table: autovacuum_vacuum_scale_factor=0.05 and autovacuum_analyze_scale_factor=0.02 for busy tables (vs defaults 0.20/0.10); check pg_stat_user_tables.

title: Create Composite Indexes for Multi-Column Queries
summary: Explains leftmost prefix rules for composite indexes and recommends placing equality-filter columns before range-filter columns for optimal multi-column query performance.
key_facts: Equality columns must come before range columns in composite index; leftmost prefix rule: WHERE status=X works, WHERE created_at>X alone does not use (status,created_at) index; 5-10x speedup.

title: Use Covering Indexes to Avoid Table Lookups
summary: Shows how to use INCLUDE clause in index definitions to cover all columns needed by a query, enabling index-only scans that skip heap fetches entirely.
key_facts: CREATE INDEX ... ON tbl(search_col) INCLUDE (col1, col2); enables index-only scan; INCLUDE columns are not searchable but are stored in index leaf pages; 2-5x speedup.

title: Choose the Right Index Type for Your Data
summary: Provides a reference guide mapping Postgres index types (B-tree, GIN, GiST, BRIN, Hash) to their supported operators and ideal use cases.
key_facts: B-tree: =,<,>,BETWEEN,IN,IS NULL. GIN: arrays,JSONB,FTS. GiST: geometry,ranges,KNN. BRIN: large time-series (10-100x smaller). Hash: equality-only slightly faster than B-tree.

title: Add Indexes on WHERE and JOIN Columns
summary: Explains how unindexed filter and join columns cause full sequential scans and shows the EXPLAIN output difference before and after adding a B-tree index.
key_facts: Always index FK columns (Postgres does NOT auto-index FK columns); Seq Scan vs Index Scan cost difference can be 100-1000x; CRITICAL priority.

title: Use Partial Indexes for Filtered Queries
summary: Shows how to create partial indexes with a WHERE clause to index only a subset of rows, producing smaller indexes and faster queries for consistently filtered columns like soft-delete flags.
key_facts: Partial index on (email) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL excludes soft-deleted rows; also useful for pending-status queues and nullable columns; 5-20x smaller index size.

title: Add Constraints Safely in Migrations
summary: Documents that PostgreSQL does not support ADD CONSTRAINT IF NOT EXISTS and provides a DO $$ block pattern using pg_constraint catalog queries to add constraints idempotently.
key_facts: ALTER TABLE ADD CONSTRAINT IF NOT EXISTS is a syntax error in PostgreSQL; use DO $$ ... if not exists (SELECT 1 FROM pg_constraint WHERE conname=...) ... $$; contype codes: p,f,u,c.

title: Choose Appropriate Data Types
summary: Provides a best-practice data type reference recommending bigint identity PKs, text over varchar(n), timestamptz over timestamp, boolean, and numeric for money.
key_facts: Always use timestamptz not timestamp; text has same performance as varchar(n); bigint identity preferred over serial; numeric(10,2) for currency; boolean is 1 byte.

title: Index Foreign Key Columns
summary: Highlights that Postgres does not auto-index FK columns and provides a diagnostic query against pg_constraint and pg_index to find all tables with missing FK indexes.
key_facts: Diagnostic SQL to find unindexed FKs via pg_constraint join pg_index; missing FK index causes full table scan on DELETE CASCADE; HIGH impact (10-100x).

title: Use Lowercase Identifiers for Compatibility
summary: Explains PostgreSQL case-folding rules and why quoted mixed-case identifiers cause tool/ORM/AI compatibility issues, recommending snake_case throughout.
key_facts: Unquoted identifiers are folded to lowercase; quoted mixed-case identifiers require quotes in every subsequent query; ORMs often generate camelCase - configure to snake_case; views can act as compatibility layer.

title: Partition Large Tables for Better Performance
summary: Shows range-based time partitioning syntax, explains partition pruning for date queries, and contrasts instantaneous DROP TABLE partition vs hours-long DELETE for old data removal.
key_facts: Partition when table >100M rows or time-series; DROP TABLE on a partition is instant vs DELETE taking hours; created_at column must be NOT NULL for range partitioning; 5-20x speedup.

title: Select Optimal Primary Key Strategy
summary: Compares serial, bigint identity, UUIDv4, and UUIDv7 primary key strategies with guidance on when to use each based on scale and distribution requirements.
key_facts: Prefer bigint generated always as identity for single DB; UUIDv7 (time-ordered) via pg_uuidv7 extension for distributed systems; avoid UUIDv4 PKs on large tables due to index fragmentation; serial works but identity is SQL-standard.

title: Apply Principle of Least Privilege
summary: Shows how to create minimal-permission roles for read-only and write-limited application access and how to revoke the default public schema permissions.
key_facts: Revoke all on schema public from public; create nologin role + grant usage on schema + grant select/insert/update on specific tables; never use superuser for app connections.

title: Enable Row Level Security for Multi-Tenant Data
summary: Explains RLS concepts and shows how to enable it on a table, create a policy using current_setting or auth.uid(), and use FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY to also apply to table owners.
key_facts: ALTER TABLE ... FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY applies policy to table owners too; policy with auth.uid() for Supabase; CRITICAL impact for multi-tenant isolation.

title: Optimize RLS Policies for Performance
summary: Shows the (select auth.uid()) wrapping trick to cache the function result once per query instead of per row, and security-definer helper function pattern for complex RLS checks.
key_facts: Wrap auth.uid() in SELECT to cache: (select auth.uid()) not auth.uid(); security definer functions must set search_path=''; always index RLS policy columns; 100x+ speedup on large tables.

title: Supabase
summary: Comprehensive Supabase skill covering core principles, CLI usage, MCP server setup, schema change workflow, and an extensive security checklist for auth, RLS, views, storage, and API key exposure.
key_facts: Never use raw_user_meta_data for authorization (user-editable); views bypass RLS by default (use security_invoker=true in PG15+); UPDATE requires SELECT policy or silently returns 0 rows; service_role key must never be in public clients; supabase db query requires CLI v2.79.0+.

title: D01 — Pipeline & Deals (Per-feature deep-dive)
summary: Deals and pipeline management feature. Two clean routes (/api/deals and /api/deals/[id]) use Pattern A (getApiRequestContext). Two broken routes use Pattern D (createServiceClient aliased → RLS bypass → 401). Critical P0 bug: quickRouteDeal at lib/treatment-routing/adapter.ts expects positional args (tenantId: string, treatmentTags: string[]) but all 7 call sites pass a single object literal, causing silent fallback to emergency routing for every form, webhook, and PMS deal. Fix recommended: make quickRoute an alias for routeDealWithAdapter accepting an object (Option B).
key_facts: P0: quickRouteDeal signature mismatch — function expects (tenantId, treatmentTags[]) but all 7 call sites pass ({...}) object — every form/webhook/PMS deal silently mis-routes; Pattern A (healthy): getApiRequestContext() used by /api/deals and /api/deals/[id]; Pattern D (broken): /api/pipelines/preferences and /api/treatment-routing/bulk-reroute import createServiceClient but call auth.getUser() which always returns null → 401; Option B fix: make quickRoute accept an object argument matching all call sites; Kanban board uses Supabase realtime subscriptions via realtime-service.ts

title: D02 — Contacts & Patients (Per-feature deep-dive)
summary: Contact management feature. Pattern D auth bug in both contact API routes: createClient at lib/supabase-server.ts:74 is aliased to createServiceClient (service-role, no cookies), so auth.getUser() always returns null and routes always 401. All contact CRUD actually happens browser-side via createClient from @/lib/supabase-client. /contacts/new is a BLOCKED redirect. Hard delete on contacts. Bulk PATCH has no role check. The app_users.role column has a CHECK constraint allowing only 3 roles (owner/manager/staff) while the rest of the system uses 5–7 roles.
key_facts: Pattern D: export const createClient = createServiceClient at lib/supabase-server.ts:74 — service-role client used with auth.getUser() → always null → 401; All contact CRUD is browser-side via @/lib/supabase-client (not server-side API); Hard delete on contacts — no soft delete / GDPR concern; Bulk PATCH has no role check; app_users.role CHECK allows only owner/manager/staff (3 roles) but system uses 5–7 roles elsewhere; Role drift across 3 membership tables is the root cause of dozens of downstream bugs

title: D03 — Communications (Email, SMS, WhatsApp) (Per-feature deep-dive)

Five separate email-provider abstraction layers exist (email-service.ts, services/email-service.ts, integrations/email-provider.ts, email-queue.ts, communications/dispatcher.ts) — extreme duplication. WhatsApp credentials stored plaintext in tenants table. No inbox/conversations view. Phase 2b prompt series (steps 6–9) was created specifically to fix these issues.
key_facts: P0: All 5 send routes have zero auth and no rate limit — anyone can send from any tenant; Inbound email webhook: no HMAC verification, trusts tenant_id from body; 5 email-provider abstraction layers causing duplication and confusion; WhatsApp credentials stored plaintext in tenants table; No inbox/conversations view for inbound messages; Phase 2b prompt series addresses these issues

title: D18 — Billing & Subscriptions (Per-feature deep-dive)

title: F01 — Authentication & Multi-Tenancy (Foundation)

Non-atomic creates (tenant + location + membership) with TODO rollback comments.

title: Index Foreign Key Columns
summary: Reference guide explaining that PostgreSQL does not auto-index foreign key columns and providing a query to find all missing FK indexes plus the corrective CREATE INDEX pattern.

title: Use Lowercase Identifiers for Compatibility
summary: Reference guide explaining why PostgreSQL identifiers should be lowercase snake_case to avoid quoting requirements and compatibility issues with ORMs, tools, and AI assistants.
key_facts: Unquoted identifiers fold to lowercase; mixed-case requires quoting forever; if stuck with mixed-case, create views as compatibility layer

title: Partition Large Tables for Better Performance
summary: Reference guide for PostgreSQL table partitioning by range (e.g., monthly time buckets), covering when to partition, syntax, and the benefit of instant partition drops for old data.
key_facts: Partition tables > 100M rows or time-series needing date-based queries; DROP TABLE on a partition is instant vs DELETE taking hours; created_at must be NOT NULL for range partitioning

title: Select Optimal Primary Key Strategy
summary: Reference guide comparing primary key strategies (IDENTITY bigint, UUIDv4, UUIDv7) and recommending bigint GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY for most cases and UUIDv7 for distributed systems.
key_facts: Prefer bigint GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY; avoid UUIDv4 as PK on large tables (index fragmentation); UUIDv7 requires pg_uuidv7 extension; serial works but IDENTITY is SQL-standard

title: Apply Principle of Least Privilege
summary: Reference guide for granting minimal, specific PostgreSQL privileges using role separation (readonly vs writer roles) and revoking default public schema access.
key_facts: Revoke all on schema public from public; create separate app_readonly and app_writer roles with explicit table-level grants; never grant ALL PRIVILEGES for application roles

title: Enable Row Level Security for Multi-Tenant Data
summary: Reference guide for enabling PostgreSQL RLS on tables with policy examples using current_setting('app.current_user_id') and auth.uid() to enforce per-user row isolation.
key_facts: Use ALTER TABLE ... FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY to protect even table owners; use (select auth.uid()) not auth.uid() in policies for performance; policy with TO authenticated uses auth.uid()

title: Optimize RLS Policies for Performance

key_facts: Wrap auth.uid() in SELECT: (select auth.uid()) to call once not per-row; SECURITY DEFINER bypasses RLS—keep in private schema, include auth.uid() check, REVOKE EXECUTE from PUBLIC; add index on RLS predicate columns
